text: Click directly on the Executive Summary's headline Total Sales card. In the Fields pane, Power BI highlights exactly which measure populates that card's Values well. Not the card's title text, which is just a label someone typed. The measure, not the title, decides the number.

Don't just stare at the Fields pane and declare victory. Add a second, test card, bound explicitly to the plain Total Sales measure, and filter the page to Pacific again. The suspect card stays unchanged. The test card changes to Pacific's actual total, and now matches the Drill-Down page. One variable changed, output changed exactly as predicted.

Here's the full mechanical explanation. Total Sales All Regions is CALCULATE of Total Sales, with ALL of TerritoryDim, which strips any filter flowing through that relationship, including this page's own Region slicer. The headline card got bound to that measure instead of the plain one, most likely a mis-drag back in Lesson 7, where both measures sit right next to each other alphabetically.

With no region selected, both measures returned the same number by coincidence, because ALL has nothing to strip away yet. That's exactly why nobody caught it when the page was first built and reviewed. The moment a real region filter gets applied, the mis-bound card keeps showing the company-wide total while everything else responds correctly.

Nothing about Total Sales All Regions is wrong — it's still needed as the denominator inside Percent of Company Total. This is a binding mistake, not a formula mistake, and that's exactly why reviewing the DAX alone would never have caught it. Next lesson: making the fix, and validating it properly.
